title: Presentability of the vertices and restricted totals of a small cellular tree
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; small means $\mathcal U$-small. Let $\tau\in\mathcal U$ be uncountable regular, meaning that a union of fewer than $\tau$ sets of size less than $\tau$ has size less than $\tau$. A category is $\tau$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\tau$ morphisms admits a cocone; for a poset, every subset of size less than $\tau$, including the empty subset, must have an upper bound. An object is $\tau$-presentable if its Hom functor preserves small $\tau$-filtered colimits. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with small Hom sets and all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Use the cellular trees, their specified cell squares, and restricted colimits of [def-coef-good-cellular-tree].

Let $L$ be an arrow class and let $D$ be an $L$-tree rooted at a $\tau$-presentable object $M$, on a small well-founded poset $T$ with $|T|<\tau$. Assume both endpoints $P_t,Q_t$ of every specified cell are $\tau$-presentable. Every vertex $D(t)$ and every restricted colimit $Y_E$ for a downward-closed $E\subseteq T$ is $\tau$-presentable. In particular every predecessor colimit and the total object $Y_T$ are $\tau$-presentable, including the empty restricted colimit $Y_\varnothing=M$.

source.place: Definition A.1.5.1 and Notation A.1.5.2, printed pp. 799-800, with the compact endpoint observation used after Lemma A.1.5.11 in Proposition A.1.5.12, printed pp. 808-809. Agent-formulated well-founded-induction lemma; the general small-colimit ingredient is Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Presentable/Limits.lean:185-195, already carried by lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable. No Stacks tag for this whole tree assertion.

proof.text: For a downward-closed $E\subseteq T$, the tree definition gives maps $r_t:M\to D(t)$ and a diagram in $M/\mathcal A$. Adjoin to its underlying diagram one new initial vertex with value $M$ and arrows $r_t$ to the vertices of $E$. A cocone on this augmented diagram with vertex $Z$ is precisely a map $u:M\to Z$ and compatible maps $v_t:D(t)\to Z$ satisfying $v_t r_t=u$. For each fixed $u$, the undercategory colimit property gives exactly one map $Y_E\to Z$ respecting these maps and the root map. Thus the underlying object of $Y_E$ has the ordinary colimit universal property for the augmented diagram. Its morphisms consist of at most one per ordered pair in $E$, one root arrow per element of $E$, and the root identity, so their cardinality is at most $|E|^2+|E|+1<\tau$: for infinite $E$ this cardinal is $|E|<\tau$, and for finite $E$ it is finite. For $E=\varnothing$, the augmented diagram consists only of $M$, giving $Y_\varnothing\cong M$.

source.place: Definition A.1.5.1 and Notation A.1.5.2, printed pp. 799-800; universal-property calculation for the undercategory colimit.

proof.text: Prove by well-founded induction on $t\in T$ that every vertex $D(t)$ is $\tau$-presentable, assuming this for all strict predecessors. Let $B_t=\{s:s<t\}$. By Step 1, the predecessor object $Y_{<t}$ is the colimit of the augmented predecessor diagram with root value $M$. Its values are $\tau$-presentable by the induction hypothesis and the assumed presentability of $M$, and its number of morphisms is less than $\tau$. The Mathlib theorem [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] therefore makes $Y_{<t}$ $\tau$-presentable. The specified cell square in [def-coef-good-cellular-tree] identifies $D(t)$ with the colimit of the finite span $Y_{<t}\leftarrow P_t\to Q_t$. All three objects are $\tau$-presentable, and the span has fewer than $\tau$ morphisms, so the same theorem makes $D(t)$ $\tau$-presentable. The case $B_t=\varnothing$ is included because the augmented predecessor diagram is then just the one-object diagram on the root.

source.place: Definition A.1.5.1 and the compact endpoint observation after Lemma A.1.5.11, printed pp. 799-800 and 808-809; well-founded induction with the finite cell pushout.

proof.text: After the induction, every value $D(t)$ is $\tau$-presentable. Apply Step 1 to any downward-closed $E\subseteq T$. The augmented diagram for $Y_E$ has fewer than $\tau$ morphisms and all its values (the root and the vertices in $E$) are $\tau$-presentable. By [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable], its colimit $Y_E$ is $\tau$-presentable. This applies in particular to every predecessor colimit and to $E=T$, while Step 1 already identifies the empty case with the assumed presentable object $M$.

source.place: Notation A.1.5.2 and Proposition A.1.5.12, printed pp. 799-800 and 808-809; closure of the restricted colimits under the same small-colimit argument.

lean.statement: theorem smallTree_presentable_vertices_and_restrictions {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [HasColimitsOfSize.{v, v} A] (τ : Cardinal.{v}) [Fact τ.IsRegular] (hτ : Cardinal.aleph0 < τ) (L : MorphismProperty A) (M : A) [IsCardinalPresentable M τ] (T : Type v) [PartialOrder T] [WellFoundedLT T] (tree : CellularTree L M T) (hT : HasCardinalLT T τ) (hcell : ∀ t : T, IsCardinalPresentable (tree.source t) τ ∧ IsCardinalPresentable (tree.target t) τ) : (∀ t : T, IsCardinalPresentable (tree.diagram.obj t).right τ) ∧ (∀ E : Set T, IsLowerSet E → IsCardinalPresentable (subsetObj tree.diagram E).right τ)
